title: Aurora Biosciences - private deploy scratchpad
content:
Quick capture from 2026-02-17 call w/ Aurora Biosciences (internal notes). Rough, keep as single-source-of-truth for followups.

Attendees (Aurora): Sara Ng (CTO), Vikram Patel (Infra lead), Mei Zhou (compliance)
Redwood: Maya (SE), Diego (deployment), Hannah (security)

High-level ask
- They want a private deployment (air-gapped option) in their lab cluster for model inference used inside R&D workflows (molecule generation prompts + multi-turn analysis).
- Hard requirement: no outbound internet from inference hosts. Control plane can be in customer VPC but must not allow egress to public internet except to our management endpoints via approved bastion (TBD).
- HSM/KMS integration mandatory; keys must be customer-controlled (FIPS/HSM preferred).
- Data residency: models and inference logs must remain on-prem, logs retained 90 days. No telemetry leaving environment unless explicitly turned on.

Workload characteristics (Aurora-provided)
- Input: short prompts ~ 30-80 tokens, often batched by internal app into 8-16 parallel requests.
- Output: generative responses ~ 150-600 tokens (varies). Typical median response ~220 tokens.
- Throughput target: sustained 40 qps during business hours, spiky up to 120 qps bursts for batch experiments.
- Latency SLO: median latency per request <= 350ms token-start (they understand long completions will exceed absolute latency but want first-token < 600ms ideally). They care more about predictability than absolute lowest latency.
- Concurrency: expected 60 concurrent user sessions during peak experiments.

Initial sizing (back-of-envelope) - assumptions: Llama-2-style 13B quantized profile, FP16 optimized kernels, NVMe-backed cache
- Baseline: 4 x A10G or 2 x A100 (40GB) per serving pool for steady 40 qps with caching + batching (estimate).
- Burst capacity: autoscale to additional nodes (policy: add 50% capacity per burst event). But note: their onprem cluster has limited spare nodes (they can add capacity from cloud provider contracts but need SOW).
- Storage: models + checkpoints ~ 120GB per model variant (they will keep 3 variants). Need ~500GB usable for model artifacts + snapshots; recommend 2TB NVMe for headroom and KV-cache storage.
- Network: 100Gb internal NICs recommended; poor NICs cause tail latency spikes.

Operational constraints / gotchas
- Air-gapped update flow: They asked for an "offline bundle" process (tarball + signature) we must implement. No remote pull allowed by default. Need documented ops playbook and an offline verification tool.
- KMS/HSM: Integration with Thales/HSM will require time; plan for 6-week integration testing. Need to know exact HSM model and APIs. Ask: do they want key use logging exported locally?
- Container images: security team only allows signed images from internal registry. We'll need to provide OCI bundles and verification steps. PRs for image generation + signing required.
- Model licensing: Aurora insists on explicit license artifact for each open model we install. We must track per-model license file in bundle and show hash in manifest.
- Telemetry: default redwood telemetry must be off. Provide customer-controlled opt-in via a local forwarder. Must show list of metrics that would be collected if enabled.
- Resource quotas: Their cluster uses Slurm-like scheduler. We need to provide guidance for GPU reservation and node labeling. Diego to draft a sample Slurm job file.

Open questions (to resolve)
- Exact GPU types available on Aurora infra? They mentioned a mix of A10G and older V100s. We need exact SKUs + driver versions.
- Compliance: Mei asked whether we support SOC2-style audit artifacts for Private deployments (answer: yes, but need to deliver logs + access records). Followup: provide sample access audit bundle.
- Model update cadence: how frequently do they want model refresh? They said "quarterly" but R&D may want weekly experiments. Clarify scope (production vs experiment).
- Can we use a small outbound allow-list to Redwood management endpoint via a controlled bastion? This would simplify control plane operations. Need legal signoff and network architecture diagram.

Next steps (action items)
- Diego: produce preliminary sizing spreadsheet (gpus, memory, disk) and recommended node counts by 2026-02-24. Add two scenarios: conservative (no KV cache, minimal batching) and optimized (prefix caching + batching).
- Maya: prepare demo plan for on-prem installer (air-gapped bundle demo) and list of deliverables for SOW by 2026-02-28. Include offline bundle format and verification steps.
- Hannah: produce KMS/HSM integration checklist and security questions to hand back to Aurora (HSM vendor + model, requirement for FIPS, key rotation policy) by 2026-02-22.
- Diego + Aurora infra: exchange current node inventory + NIC speeds + driver versions. Need by 2026-02-20 (urgency: high).
- Hana (Aurora): send sample R&D workload traces (token length distribution, request rate CSV) to help refine batching suggestions.

Risks / assumptions
- Assume they will allow us to run a management agent (read-only) on a bastion for control-plane ops. If not allowed, operational overhead increases significantly and SOW will expand.
- Assume models will remain open-source; if they require proprietary models we need different licensing path and additional storage.

Notes to self
- Build an offline-demo playbook: 1) build model tar.gz + manifest (hash + license) 2) sign with Redwood offline key (or provide signing tool) 3) customer verifies signature using provided public key 4) install via local CLI 5) run health checks (latency/throughput smoke).
- Keep examples of signed manifests in the repo PR (link above).
- Add a short slide on "what we need from Aurora" for next call: exact GPU SKUs, network diagram, HSM vendor info, desired model variants, and which apps are high-priority.

Meeting copy-paste snippets (raw):
- Sara: "We cannot have any outbound telemetry by default. That's a dealbreaker."
- Vikram: "If the management plane needs a heartbeat we can allow it through our bastion, but it must be authenticated and logged."
- Mei: "Our legal team will need to see the offline bundle signing process and model license tracking before we sign anything."

Follow-up call: propose week of 2026-03-01 (align with Diego availability). Will do internal prep doc + demo checklist beforehand.

-- end scratchpad --
